SECTION 0. ANALYSIS OVERVIEW

0-1. Archetype Determination [Decision]
Primary archetype: **B — Quality Compounder.** Secondary character: **Cyclical**
(semiconductor revenue cycle) with an **option-like overlay** (AI data-centre power
franchise). Declared as a Blended position: Engine 1 × 75%, Engine 2 × 25%; Engine 4
applied as a *reverse-DCF test*, not as a value contributor.

0-2. Why B, not D (Product-Platform Hybrid), and not E (Option-Led)
1. Revenue is *component sales into sockets*, not a monetised installed base. MPWR has no
   recurring/subscription revenue, no attach-rate economics and no installed-base
   monetisation. Engine 3 requires a Platform Feature Score that cannot be evidenced
   from this pack: segment revenue and margin by business line are not held (SECTION 12).
   Building a "platform premium" here would violate Final Rule 7.
2. Capital intensity, margin structure and ROIC are those of a fabless quality analog
   franchise, not of a hardware-plus-platform hybrid. Gross margin has printed between
   54.1% (FY2014) and 58.5% (FY2022) for twelve consecutive years — a ±2.2pp band around
   55%. That is elite analog-franchise stability [Arithmetic on filed SECTION 5].
3. Adjusted ROIC 24.4% against a 12.5% WACC is a ~12pp spread sustained for a decade —
   the defining Quality Compounder test [Estimate, Layer 2.5].

0-3. Why not Engine 5 (binary) — no single approval event. Why not Engine 4 alone — the
company has $2.79B of filed FY2025 revenue and 12 years of GAAP profitability. An
option-only valuation would ignore ~$0.48B of owner earnings that actually exist.

0-4. Transition assessment: MPWR is in a **B → D transition** at the narrative level
("chip company" → "semiconductor-based solution providers", management, Q2-2026 call).
Criteria met: none of the Engine-3 platform tests can be verified from held data.
Criteria NOT met: recurring monetisation (0% of revenue), installed-base economics,
ecosystem lock-in. Assessment: **transition not established; narrative ahead of
evidence.** Per Step 0-3, this is recorded as a transition period → **Conviction -0.5**.

0-5. Data-quality findings surfaced BEFORE modelling (these change the answer; they are
not footnotes):
(a) **FY2024 net income of $1.592B is not an operating figure.** Q4-2024 alone printed
    $1.449B of net income on $0.622B of revenue [Arithmetic on SECTION 4]. FY2024 net

    forecast anchored on FY2024 net income is wrong by ~$1.3B.**
(b) **The pack's "change in working capital" column is contaminated by cash flows.**
    It is computed as current assets minus current liabilities; current assets *include
    cash and short-term investments*. FY2025 prints +$0.544B of ΔWC — 93% of that year's
    $0.583B revenue increment — because cash rose $0.407B and short-term investments fell
    $0.424B [Arithmetic on SECTION 6 and 6B]. Feeding that column into a DCF overstates
    the cash drag roughly fourfold. I rebuilt operating WC from the receivables and
    inventory lines only: FY2025 operaging-WC build was $0.228B, i.e. ~39% of the revenue
    increment. All subsequent modelling uses the rebuilt figure.
(c) **The vendor SBC scalar ($0.227B, SECTION 2) is a fiscal-year figure, not TTM** — it
    matches the filed FY2025 series exactly. Confirmed, and the filed series is used.
(d) **Debt is unresolved by component.** Long-term debt is carried as "not available" for
    all twelve years; the vendor scalar is $0.020B. I use $0.020B and state the ambiguity.
    It is immaterial either way: the company is structurally net cash.
(e) **FY2027 consensus is internally contradictory.** Yahoo Finance (2026-07-09) implies

0-6. Model Confidence: **Medium-High on the business, Medium-Low on the price.**

material Tier 4/5 dependencies are (i) the AI data-centre power revenue path beyond FY2027
and (ii) capex intensity during the capacity expansion. Both are disclosed *directionally*
(capacity extended "beyond $6B"; enterprise-data growth floor raised 85%→130%) and

1-2. Regime probability distribution [Assumption, reasoned from the retrieved set]

| Regime | Probability | Rationale |

| Recession (low rates + low growth) | 10% | Not priced by the curve; small residual |

| Axis | Score | Reasoning |

Goldilocks 0 | Reflation +4 | Stagflation -1 | Recession -5

sensitivity both work against the position simultaneously. This is a macro regime where a

1.5-2. Deviation of my conclusion from the base rate
My probability-implied bull case (see SECTION 4) is 25%, against an unconditional base
rate of ~5–10% for the underlying outcome. That is a **2.5x–5x deviation**, which triggers
Step 1.5-3. Three company-specific justifications are required; I supply four:
1. **Forward visibility is contractual, not narrative.** Q3-CY2026 revenue guidance is
   $1.14–1.16B versus an analyst estimate of $986.8M (StockStory; Quartr) — a ~17%
   guided sequential increase over an already record Q2. Book-to-bill remained "well
   above 1" (Q2-2026 call).
2. **Management is making a costly, hard-to-reverse commitment.** Capacity goals
   were "extended significantly beyond $6 billion" (Q2-2026 call). Capital commitments of
   that kind are informative precisely because they are expensive to reverse.
3. **Additive SAMs are entering, not substituting.** Initial DDR5 high-speed interface
   controller orders received, expected to expand SAM "through 2027"; 800V AC-DC products
   in sampling for 800V data-centre architectures; in-house GaN development.
4. **Share gains are documented against disclosed internal targets.** CPU-server share has
   "exceeded its internal target of 30%"; >1,500 new automotive sockets shipped YTD.

1.5-3. Base-rate shock verdict
Success probability is 2.5x–5x the unconditional base rate. **RED FLAG RAISED AND
RE-EVALUATED.** Resolution: the unconditional base rate is the wrong reference class. The
correct conditional class is "semis growing >40% with book-to-bill >1 and capacity being
expanded." Conditional on that information set, a 25% bull probability is defensible.
**However**, per the framework's own rule, 2.0x+ requires the deviation to be *carried as
a risk*, not netted away. It is carried: it is the reason SECTION 4's bear probability is
28% rather than 20%, and it is the reason SECTION 5's conviction is capped.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SECTION 2. BUSINESS QUALITY

2-1. What the company does (3 sentences)
MPWR designs and sells power-management integrated circuits and power modules —
DC-DC converters, power stages, controllers, and increasingly complete vertical power
delivery solutions — selling fabless through foundries and assembly partners.
It sells into five end markets: enterprise data (AI/GPU and server core power), automotive,
communications (optical modules, switches, TPUs, NICs), industrial, and consumer.
Its economic engine is the design-in socket: winning a component position inside a
customer's next-generation board (2–5 year cycle), then holding it.

Understandability: **High** for the business model; **Low-to-Medium** for the AI
data-centre power TAM and competitive structure, where the required inputs (hyperscaler
capex intentions, 800V HVDC vendor allocation) are Tier 5 — [Unconfirmed] probability
distributions. Analysis reliability on the *core* is high; on the *growth option* it is
materially lower. This asymmetry is central to SECTION 3.

2-2. Moat assessment + moat dynamics (0–3 each)

|---|---|---|---|
| Intangible assets (patents/process) | 2 | Stable | In-house GaN development; proprietary BOM/module integration |

| Data moat | 1 | Widening | Design-win database; motion-control/robotics IP applied internally |
| **Total** | **10 / 21** | **Narrow-to-Wide, widening** | |

Moat verdict: **Narrow-to-Wide.** The switching-cost sub-score is the highest possible and

2-3. Lynch classification
**Fast Grower** (revenue CAGR trailing 5 FY: +27.0%, [Arithmetic]). Fast Growers are
governed by one checkpoint that matters more than the rest: the *sustainability of the

- Margin direction: positive (operating margin 12.4% FY2014 → 26.1% FY2025 → 31.0% in

- Repeat-buyer/socket stickiness: strong (switching costs 3/3). Good.
- Inventory/saturation risk: **elevated**. 157 days of inventory at Q1-2026 (Q2 call);

2.5-1. R&D capitalisation [Estimate — R&D is NOT a held line]

R&D + other = Gross profit − SG&A − Operating income.

| FY | GP | SG&A | OI | Implied R&D+other | % of revenue |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2022 | 1.049 | 0.282 | 0.527 | 0.240 | 13.4% |
| 2023 | 1.021 | 0.276 | 0.482 | 0.263 | 14.4% |
| 2024 | 1.221 | 0.357 | 0.539 | 0.325 | 14.7% |
| 2025 | 1.540 | 0.429 | 0.729 | 0.382 | 13.7% |

Assume a 4-year amortisation life and FY2022 R&D ≈ $0.240B.
Unamortised R&D pool at FY2025 = 0.25(0.240) + 0.50(0.263) + 0.75(0.325) + 1.00(0.382)
= 0.060 + 0.132 + 0.244 + 0.382 = **$0.818B**.
FY2025 amortisation charge = 0.818 / 4 = **$0.205B**.
Adjusted operating income = 0.729 + 0.382 − 0.205 = **$0.906B**.

FY2025 SBC $0.227B = 8.1% of revenue = 36.6% of net income.
Adjusted FCF (OCF − capex − SBC) = 0.838 − 0.172 − 0.227 = **$0.439B**
→ **SBC-adjusted FCF yield on T0 market cap = 0.74%**
TTM equivalent: 0.586 − ~0.250 = ~$0.34B → **0.57%**.
> This is the single most important number in the report for the *price* question. On the

> than a 1% cash yield.
> Note for consistency: my DCF (SECTION 3) starts from *GAAP operating income*, which

FY2025 $0.024B — 0.04% of market cap. Immaterial. Included in net debt for completeness.

MPWR sells components to engineers, not to consumers. There is no separable,
defensible brand asset, and no data asset with a measurable unit price. Forced
capitalisation here would manufacture value. Assigned zero, explicitly.

**+11.9pp spread.** This is the strongest single fact in the long case.

| **Owner-earnings yield at $1,203.75** | **0.81%** |

Range: $0.44–0.48B across defensible payables assumptions → **0.75%–0.81%**.
For the price to imply a 4% owner-earnings yield, owner earnings would have to be
**$2.37B — five times the current level.** That is the expectations gap in one sentence.

3.5-1. Competitive response simulation — **net -2**
The AI data-centre power socket is now the highest-priority target of every large analog
and power vendor: Texas Instruments, Analog Devices, Infineon, Renesas, STMicro, onsemi,
Vicor, Navitas, Power Integrations. NVIDIA's published 800V HVDC architecture names a

you the architecture is **multi-vendor by design** — hyperscalers demand second sources.
Consequences that the sell-side narrative omits:
- The SAM grows, but the *share per vendor is structurally capped*.
- Multi-sourcing plus a public architecture accelerates ASP erosion.
- MPWR's own "full-solution provider" transition requires it to build software, modules and
  reference designs — raising the cost to compete against vendors with larger scale.
Direction: **-2.** The competitive response is not speculative; it is already the stated
strategy of every competitor.

3.5-2. Reflexivity check (Soros) — **asymmetric, net -1**
Positive loop, currently live: a $1,204 price supports talent retention through SBC, gives
MPWR acquisition currency, and confers customer credibility as a "full solution provider."
Negative loop, latent and larger: SBC is **8.1% of revenue and 36.6% of net income**. A
prolonged de-rating does not merely annoy employees — it impairs the compensation mechanism
that funds the R&D engine itself. The positive loop is a *marketing* effect; the negative
loop is an *operating* effect. Both cannot be true at equal magnitude; the negative is
larger.

3.5-3. Customer behaviour evolution — **net -0.5**
Early adopter → mainstream → late adopter across MPWR's five end markets is proceeding
unevenly. Automotive skews late-adopter in nature (5-year sockets → the lowest churn, the
most durable LTV). Consumer/notebook is explicitly weak and getting weaker (management:
"I think the notebook side of storage and compute will continue to remain cautious").
Industrial is "lagging… focus on a multiyear design-win cycle rather than immediate
revenue." So the mix is rotating toward the two extremes: durable automotive and
hyper-cyclical AI data centre, while the middle (industrial, consumer) is soft. Rising
penetration in AI data centre means CAC rises as MPWR must build full solutions. Net
LTV/CAC is stable-to-worsening, not improving.

**Step 3.5-1. Competitive response simulation: SCORE −2 (net negative).**
If MPWR succeeds, it succeeds by taking power-delivery content away from Texas Instruments,
Analog Devices, Infineon, Renesas and Vicor — and, more dangerously, by occupying a socket
that hyperscalers would rather own themselves. The rational responses are: (i) price
aggression from TI's new 300mm analog capacity [Unconfirmed — not retrieved]; (ii) vertical
integration by the customer — the very 800V/vertical-power architecture MPWR is sampling
into *invites* the accelerator vendor to specify and eventually design the power stage;
(iii) second-sourcing mandates, which are standard hyperscaler procurement practice. MPWR's
own management notes the enterprise-data business "does not have customer concentration"
[Actual] — which cuts both ways: no single customer can hurt them, but no single customer
will protect them either, and none will resist the urge to dual-source.

**Step 3.5-2. Reflexivity check: SCORE −1 (mildly negative asymmetry).**
The high share price is *not* a funding advantage (net cash, no need to issue) and *is* a
cost: 8.1% of revenue goes out as SBC into a stock whose price is elevated, and the new
$500M buyback authorisation will retire shares at ~44x earnings. Asymmetry: a falling stock
does not threaten solvency or customer confidence (net cash, diversified customers), but a
falling stock *does* make SBC less attractive to talent. Meanwhile the reflexivity that
matters runs the other way — high stock price → high SBC expense → dilution → per-share
growth below net-income growth. 3-yr net share issuance of +1.8% [Actual] is the evidence.

**Step 3.5-3. Customer behaviour evolution: SCORE −1.**
AI datacenter power is moving from early-adopter (single-source, performance-first) to
mainstream (multi-source, cost-and-supply-first). That transition historically compresses
ASP per watt and per socket even as unit volumes rise. When MSP grows 48% YoY and gross
margin does not move (55.2% → 55.2%) [Actual], the mechanism is already visible: the module
/full-solution pivot carries more bill-of-materials per dollar of revenue. Management's
own framing — "from a chip company to a semiconductor-based solution provider," plus
building its own GaN and its own back-end assembly — is structurally *lower*-margin than
selling an IC.
